inventory.name: WindowClient.navigate() from service workers — the affected method surface: when the WindowClient is a subframe and the target URL resolves to a local/private address, the call now triggers an LNA permission check; main-frame navigations are unchanged

Subframe LNA check on WindowClient.navigate() — the initiator-based decision the page enumerates: main-frame clients are exempt; a subframe client's own origin is the navigation initiator; a public initiator triggers the LNA permission check; an ungranted permission or insecure context blocks the navigation

syntax.rationale: No new grammar ships with this change — Chrome 147 attaches LNA enforcement to the existing WindowClient.navigate(url) method — so syntax is earned by the real call form a reader writes, the client.navigate() invocation in the what-changes pre/code example, not by the section's inline identifier mentions (coord ruling 2(b)).

The check is an enforcement algorithm with no declarable surface of its own and no new API is introduced; syntax is anchored to the same example because the navigate() call there is the call whose execution runs the check — the section's inline code mentions alone would not be a grammar (coord ruling 2(b)).
